claims.claim: CAFE standards were first enacted by Congress in 1975, in response to the 1973-74 Arab oil embargo, to improve the average fuel economy of cars and light trucks.
claims.episode_span: The law had been written to reduce oil consumption after the 1973 embargo
claims.supporting_quote: Corporate average fuel economy ( CAFE ) standards are regulations in the United States, first enacted by the United States Congress in 1975, [ 1 ] after the 1973–74 Arab Oil Embargo , to improve the average fuel economy of cars and light trucks (trucks, vans and sport utility vehicles ) produced for sale in the United States.

claims.claim: President Gerald Ford signed the Energy Policy and Conservation Act into law on December 22, 1975.
claims.episode_span: In December 1975 President Gerald Ford signed the Energy Policy and Conservation Act
claims.source_title: Energy Policy and Conservation Act - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: Signed into law by President Gerald Ford on December 22, 1975

claims.claim: EPCA set car fuel-economy standards of 18, 19, and 20 mpg for model years 1978-1980 and required a 27.5 mpg average by 1985.
claims.episode_span: Lawmakers set an initial target of 27.5 miles per gallon for passenger cars by model year 1985
claims.source_title: Energy Policy and Conservation Act - Wikipedia
claims.supporting_quote: The average fuel economy for model years, 1978, 1979, and 1980 were set at 18, 19, and 20 miles per gallon, respectively, and by 1985 the average economy was required to be 27.5 mpg.

claims.claim: The Dodge Caravan was introduced alongside the Plymouth Voyager in November 1983 for the 1984 model year.
claims.episode_span: In 1983 Chrysler certified the Caravan and Voyager as trucks
claims.supporting_quote: the Dodge Caravan was introduced alongside the Plymouth Voyager in November 1983 for the 1984 model year

claims.claim: In July 2011 President Obama announced an agreement with automakers to raise fuel economy to 54.5 mpg for cars and light trucks by model year 2025.
claims.episode_span: The Obama administration later tightened the rules further, projecting a 54.5 mpg fleet average by 2025.
claims.supporting_quote: On July 29, 2011, President Obama announced an agreement with thirteen large automakers to increase fuel economy to 54.5 miles per gallon for cars and light-duty trucks by model year 2025.

claims.claim: CAFE standards became attribute-based, expressed as mathematical functions of vehicle footprint (wheelbase times average track width), starting in 2011.
claims.episode_span: directing NHTSA to set attribute-based standards that varied with vehicle footprint
claims.supporting_quote: Starting in 2011, the CAFE standards are newly expressed as mathematical functions depending on vehicle footprint, a measure of vehicle size determined by multiplying the vehicle's wheelbase by its average track width.
